title: Tenant-priority temporal quota allocator and invoice explainability
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem statement: Customers on Dedicated plans sometimes see temporary throughput boosts (surge events) that consume headroom and then receive invoices with opaque overage line items. This ticket implements a time-aware quota allocator that: 1) surfaces priority and temporal allocation decisions during a surge event, 2) enforces graceful proportional throttles when headroom is exhausted, and 3) emits invoice-facing explainability metadata so billing and support can attribute charges to discrete surge windows. Goal: reduce invoice disputes by 50% for burst-related charges and keep p99 latency SLOs for high-priority tenants during short surges.
acceptance_criteria: A1: The temporal quota allocator assigns surge tokens in discrete windows (<= 5min) and honors tenant priority weights set by Dedicated contracts.
A2: When burst capacity goes above contracted allocation, the allocator returns a structured reason_code and lease_id at request-time for tracing (exposed in logs and Console).
A3: Console shows a human-readable timeline for each invoice overage line that maps tokens/seconds to surge windows and lease_ids.
A4: Automated invoice reconciler can group overage charges by lease_id and produce line-level explanations in customer emails and support UI.
A5: In synthetic load tests, high-priority tenants retain >= 95% of pre-surge throughput and p99 latency regression is < 30% compared to baseline.
A6: Unit and integration tests cover allocator fairness, lease expiry, and rehydration after controller restart.
technical_design: Overview: introduce a temporal quota allocator service (TQA) that manages short-lived 'lease' tokens representing burst capacity. Leases are small (e.g., 1-5 minute TTL) and issued from a global surge pool per region. The TQA uses a priority-weighted allocator that consumes pool tokens by tenant weight and recent usage profile. Key components: 1) Lease issuance API (issue_lease), 2) Fast-path lease validation library in the serving runtime (local cache + fallback to TQA), 3) Lease ledger emitted to the event pipeline for billing/console attribution. Allocation algorithm: weighted fair share over sliding windows with decay — maintain per-tenant score = base_weight * (1 + recent_usage_factor)^{-alpha} to reduce runaway grabs. When pool depleted, allocator performs proportional yield: returns a soft-throttle decision with suggested retry-after and an opaque lease_id referencing the window that caused the decision. Billing: leases carry metadata (lease_id, window_start, window_end, pool_snapshot_id, weight_snapshot) which gets persisted into the ledger and consumed by billing reconciler to create explainable invoice lines.
backend_notes: Implementation plan: - Add TQA microservice in dedicated control plane namespace. - Use existing region-config map for pool sizes; initial pools seeded from capacity signals (ops-config). - Persist ledger events to topic 'tqa.leases.v1' with compacted key=lease_id. - Extend existing billing pipeline consumer to join lease events with token usage (per-request token_count) and emit grouped overage entries. - Introduce deterministic lease_id format: <region>-<window_ts>-<randomsuffix>. - Instrument metrics: leases_issued, leases_denied, avg_lease_duration, lease_reconciliation_lag. Operational concerns: TQA must be horizontally autoscalable and keep strict tail latency (<50ms median) for lease checks; fallback path from runtime to degrade gracefully when TQA is unreachable (local cache TTL and conservative deny strategy).
frontend_notes: Console changes: - New 'Burst timeline' panel on Dedicated tenant pages showing colored bands per lease window with hover-to-see metadata (lease_id, pool_snapshot, tenant_weight, consumed_tokens). - Invoice detail page: when an overage line has lease metadata, render 'Explain' link that expands a timeline mapping tokens->leases. - Support UI: add 'lease_id' filter to logs and troubleshooting flow. UX: show clear language for customers: 'Temporary surge lease: this overage occurred during a short regional surge window; you were charged according to the Dedicated burst policy. Click for timeline.'
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): Deploy TQA in staging and a single canary region; enable for internal tenants only; validate ledger consumer correctness and Console rendering. Phase 2 (pilot, 4 weeks): Opt-in for 5 select customers (PM identified); collect feedback on invoice explainability. Phase 3 (general availability): Gradual ramp to all Dedicated customers with default ON for new contracts; provide opt-out toggle for legacy customers for first 30 days. Monitoring during rollout: monitor 'invoice_disputes_count', 'support_ticket_latency_related_to_billing', and 'lease_reconciliation_lag'.
test_plan: Unit tests for allocator math and lease expiry. Integration tests: - Simulate concurrent lease requests from 1k tenants and validate weighted fairness. - Chaos test: TQA process restart during active window; ensure runtime cache and fallback produce consistent decisions. - Billing E2E: create synthetic surge event, ensure billing pipeline groups usage by lease_id and produces single explainable line in the invoice preview. Load tests: emulate 10x normal surge load to validate TQA tail latency and ledger throughput.
